home.storyP1: Coffee Roots started as one machine and four tables on Bogenbai Batyr Street — a bet that Almaty wanted its coffee slower, lighter, and closer to the people who grew it.
home.storyP2: Today the room is bigger but the idea isn't: single-origin beans on rotation, reclaimed wood, morning light, and enough quiet outlets that nobody asks you to leave.

about.title: A small room with tall windows
about.story1: Coffee Roots opened on Bogenbai Batyr Street with one machine, four tables, and a conviction that Almaty didn't need another place to grab coffee — it needed a place to stay with it. The first winter, regulars outnumbered chairs. We took the hint and knocked through to the room next door.
about.story2: What hasn't changed: beans roasted light enough to taste where they grew, milk steamed to order rather than by habit, and a room that runs on morning light for most of the day.
about.missionText: Make specialty coffee feel ordinary — something you have every day, in a room that treats your time as well as your cup.

v1.title: Craft without ceremony
v1.body: Precision in the cup, none of the gatekeeping. If you want to know why your filter tastes like apricot, we'll tell you — if you just want good coffee, that's the whole point.

v2.title: Room to stay
v2.body: Nobody hovers over your table. Long mornings, slow laptops, second refills — the room is designed for people who settle in, not pass through.

v3.title: Direct to the grower
v3.body: We pay producers directly and publish what's in the hopper. Better prices at origin make better coffee here — it's not charity, it's how quality works.

about.sourcing1: Two single origins rotate through the hopper every season — one washed, one natural — bought through direct-trade relationships rather than the commodity market. When a lot runs out, it's gone; we'd rather change the card on the grinder than stretch a coffee past its best.
about.sourcing2: Espresso stays consistent; filter is where we experiment. If something unusual lands — a honey-processed lot, an experimental fermentation — it shows up on the V60 bar first.
about.room1: Natural light over fixtures, reclaimed wood over laminate, and acoustics tuned so a full room still sounds like a murmur. The window bench catches sun until mid-afternoon; the back corners stay quiet, with outlets at every seat.
about.room2: It's deliberately a room for remote workers as much as for dates and long conversations — stay as long as the coffee keeps coming.
